We need to show that when Enum-Uncertain-MC is called with $C'$, the generated $X'$ which is passed in Enum-Uncertain-MC contains $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Take u < m valid for X'; need u in X'.

nodes.name: u enters X
nodes.statement: Firstly, note that since $C' \cup \{ u \}$ is $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$, we have $clq(C \cup \{ u \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$ (from Observation~\ref{obs:Sub}). Since $u > \max(C)$ and $clq(C \cup \{ u \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$, from Lemma~\ref{obs:I}, $u$ will be used in line~\ref{algoline:loop} to call Enum-Uncertain-MC using $C \cup \{ u \}$. Once this call is returned, $u$ is added to $X$ in line~\ref{algoline:addX}. Note that since the loop at line~\ref{algoline:loop} add vertices in lexicographical order, $m$ will be added to $C$ after $u$. Thus $u$ will be in $X$, when $m$ is used to extend $C$.
nodes.statement_short: By Observation 2 and Lemma 6, u is explored before m and then added to X.

nodes.name: u passes to X'
nodes.statement: Next we show that if $u \in X$, after execution of line~\ref{algoline:genX}, $u \in X'$. We prove this as follows. Note that Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateX} is used to generate $X'$ from $X$. Note that $X'$ is generated by Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateX} by selectively adding vertices from $X$. A vertex is added to $X'$ from $X$, only if $C' \cup \{ u \}$ is $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. From our initial assumptions, we know that $u$ satisfies this condition and is hence added to $X'$ and passed on to Enum-Uncertain-MC when it is called with $C'$.
nodes.statement_short: GenerateX keeps u in X'.

nodes.name: How X' is formed
nodes.statement: We prove this as follows. Note that Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateX} is used to generate $X'$ from $X$. Note that $X'$ is generated by Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateX} by selectively adding vertices from $X$.
nodes.statement_short: X' is a filtered copy of X.

nodes.name: Filter keeps u
nodes.statement: A vertex is added to $X'$ from $X$, only if $C' \cup \{ u \}$ is $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. From our initial assumptions, we know that $u$ satisfies this condition and is hence added to $X'$ and passed on to Enum-Uncertain-MC when it is called with $C'$.
nodes.statement_short: u passes the alpha-clique filter.

nodes.name: Invalid vertices excluded
nodes.statement:
Now let us consider $v$, such that $v$ does not satisfy all the conditions for $v \in X'$. We need to show that $v 
ot \in X'$. There are two cases. First, when $v 
ot \in X$. This case is trivial as $X'$ is constructed from $X$ and hence if $v 
ot \in X$, $v 
ot \in X'$. For the second case, when $v \in X$, we need to show that $v$ will not be added to $X'$ in line~ef{algoline:genX} of Algorithm~ef{algo:dfs}. Note that since $v \in X$, we know $v 
ot \in C'$ and $v < \max(C')$. Thus, it must be that $C \cup \{ m, v \}$ is not an $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. Algorithm~ef{algo:generateX} will add $v$ to $X'$ only if $C \cup \{ m, v \}$ is $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. But from our previous discussion, we know that this condition doesn't hold. Hence, $v$ will not be added to $X'$. Thus only vertices that satisfy all three conditions are in $X'$.
nodes.statement_short: Show invalid v never enter X', by two cases.

nodes.name: Two cases
nodes.statement: Now let us consider $v$, such that $v$ does not satisfy all the conditions for $v \in X'$. We need to show that $v \not \in X'$. There are two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the exclusion claim.

nodes.name: v not in X
nodes.statement:
First, when $v 
ot \in X$. This case is trivial as $X'$ is constructed from $X$ and hence if $v 
ot \in X$, $v 
ot \in X'$.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial: X' is built from X.

nodes.name: v in X
nodes.statement: For the second case, when $v \in X$, we need to show that $v$ will not be added to $X'$ in line~\ref{algoline:genX} of Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs}. Note that since $v \in X$, we know $v \not \in C'$ and $v < \max(C')$. Thus, it must be that $C \cup \{ m, v \}$ is not an $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateX} will add $v$ to $X'$ only if $C \cup \{ m, v \}$ is $\alpha$-clique in $\mathcal{G}$. But from our previous discussion, we know that this condition doesn't hold. Hence, $v$ will not be added to $X'$.
nodes.statement_short: GenerateX rejects v since C plus m,v is not an alpha-clique.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus only vertices that satisfy all three conditions are in $X'$.
nodes.statement_short: X' is exactly the valid set.

nodes.name: C is an alpha-clique
nodes.statement: Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs} emits $C$ in Line~\ref{algoline:out}. From Observation~\ref{obs:cliqueprob}, we know that $C$ is an $\alpha$-clique.
nodes.statement_short: By Observation 4 the emitted C is an alpha-clique.

nodes.name: Assume non-maximal
nodes.statement: We need to show that $C$ is $\alpha$-maximal. We use proof by contradiction. Suppose $C$ is non-maximal. This means that there exists a vertex $u \in V$, such that $C \cup \{u\}$ is an $\alpha$-clique.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose some u extends C.

nodes.name: No larger extension
nodes.statement: We know that $I = \emptyset$ when $C$ is emitted. From Lemma~\ref{obs:I}, we know that there exists no vertex $u \in V$ such that $u > max(C)$ that can extend $C$.
nodes.statement_short: I empty and Lemma 6: no larger extension.

nodes.name: No smaller extension
nodes.statement: Again, we know that $X = \emptyset$ when $C$ is emitted. Thus from Lemma~\ref{obs:X}, we know that there exists no vertex $v \in V$ such that $v < \max(C)$ that can extend $C$.
nodes.statement_short: X empty and Lemma 7: no smaller extension.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: This is a contradiction and hence $C$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique.
nodes.statement_short: So C is alpha-maximal.

nodes.name: Strengthened statement
nodes.statement: We first show that a call to method Enum-Uncertain-MC with $\alpha$-clique $C$ enumerates all $\alpha$-maximal cliques $C'$ in $\mathcal{G}$, such that for all $c \in \{ C' \setminus C \}$, $c > \max(C)$.
nodes.statement_short: Show a call with C enumerates every alpha-maximal clique extending C by larger vertices.

nodes.name: Reduce to reaching C'
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, consider a $\alpha$-maximal clique $C'$ in $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\forall c \in \{C' \setminus C \}$, $c > \max(C)$. Note that $C'$ will be emitted as an $\alpha$-maximal clique by the method Enum-Uncertain-MC when called with $C$, if the following holds: (1) A call to method Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C'$, (2) When this call is made, $I' = \emptyset$, and $X' = \emptyset$. Since $C'$ is $\alpha$-maximal clique in $\mathcal{G}$, the second point follows from Lemmas~\ref{obs:I}~and~\ref{obs:X}. Thus we need to show that a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C'$.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemmas 6-7 it suffices that a call with C' is made.

nodes.name: Induction on added vertices
nodes.statement: We prove this by induction. Let $\hat{C} = \{ C' \setminus C \}$. Let $c_i$ represent the $i$th element in $\hat{C}$ in lexicographical order. Also let $C_i = C \cup \{ c_{1}, c_{2}, \ldots, c_i \}$. For the base case, we show that if a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C$, a call will be made with $C_1 = C \cup \{ c_1 \}$. This is because, line~\ref{algoline:loop} of the method loops over every vertex $u \in I$ thus implying $u > \max(C)$ and $clq(C \cup \{ u \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$. Since $C'$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique, $c_1$ will satisfy both these conditions and hence a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C \cup \{ c_1 \}$. Now for the inductive step we show that if a call is made with clique $C_i$, then this call will in turn call the method with clique $C_{i+1}$. Again, $c_{i+1}$ is greater than $\max(C_i)$ and $clq(C_i \cup \{ c_{i+1} \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$. Thus $c_{i+1} \in I$ when the call is made to Enum-Uncertain-MC with $C_i$. Hence using the previous argument, in line~\ref{algoline:loop}, $c_{i+1}$ will be used as a vertex in the loop which would in turn make a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC with $C_{i+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction along the vertices of C' \ C in order.

nodes.name: Order the new vertices
nodes.statement: We prove this by induction. Let $\hat{C} = \{ C' \setminus C \}$. Let $c_i$ represent the $i$th element in $\hat{C}$ in lexicographical order. Also let $C_i = C \cup \{ c_{1}, c_{2}, \ldots, c_i \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Let C_i add the first i new vertices.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: For the base case, we show that if a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C$, a call will be made with $C_1 = C \cup \{ c_1 \}$. This is because, line~\ref{algoline:loop} of the method loops over every vertex $u \in I$ thus implying $u > \max(C)$ and $clq(C \cup \{ u \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$. Since $C'$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique, $c_1$ will satisfy both these conditions and hence a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is made with $C \cup \{ c_1 \}$.
nodes.statement_short: c_1 is in I, so C plus c_1 is called.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: Now for the inductive step we show that if a call is made with clique $C_i$, then this call will in turn call the method with clique $C_{i+1}$. Again, $c_{i+1}$ is greater than $\max(C_i)$ and $clq(C_i \cup \{ c_{i+1} \},\mathcal{G}) \ge \alpha$. Thus $c_{i+1} \in I$ when the call is made to Enum-Uncertain-MC with $C_i$. Hence using the previous argument, in line~\ref{algoline:loop}, $c_{i+1}$ will be used as a vertex in the loop which would in turn make a call to Enum-Uncertain-MC with $C_{i+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: c_{i+1} is in I at C_i, so C_{i+1} is called.

nodes.name: Apply with C empty
nodes.statement: Now without any loss of generality, consider an $\alpha$-maximal clique in $\mathcal{G}$. We know that $C \supset \emptyset$. Thus the proof follows.
nodes.statement_short: Take C empty.

nodes.name: Search tree
nodes.statement: MULE initializes variables and calls to Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs}, hence we analyze the runtime of Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs}. An execution of the recursive Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs} can be viewed as a search tree as follows. Each call to Enum-Uncertain-MC is a node of this search tree. The first call to the method is the root node. A node in this search tree is either an internal node that makes one or more recursive calls, or a leaf node that does not make further recursive calls. To analyze the runtime of Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs}, we consider the time spent at internal nodes as well as leaf nodes.
nodes.statement_short: View the recursion as a search tree.

nodes.name: Leaf cost
nodes.statement: The runtime at each leaf node is $O(1)$. For a leaf node, the parameter $I = \emptyset$, and there are no further recursive calls. This implies that either $C$ is $\alpha$-maximal ($X = \emptyset$) and is emitted in line~\ref{algoline:out} or it is non-maximal ($X \neq \emptyset$) but cannot be extended by the loop in line~\ref{algoline:loop} as $I = \emptyset$. Checking the sizes of $I$ and $X$ takes constant time.
nodes.statement_short: O(1) per leaf.

nodes.name: Edge cost
nodes.statement: We next consider the time taken at each internal node. Instead of adding up the times at different internal nodes, we equivalently add up the cost of the different edges in the search tree. At each internal node, the cost of making a recursive call can be analyzed as follows. Line~\ref{algoline:genc} takes $O \left ( n \right )$ time as we add all vertices in $C$ to $C'$ and also $u$. Line~\ref{algoline:prob} takes constant time. Lines~\ref{algoline:genI}~and~\ref{algoline:genX} take $O \left ( n \right )$ time (Lemmas~\ref{lemma:complexity1}~and~\ref{lemma:complexity2} respectively). Note that lines~\ref{algoline:genc}~to~\ref{algoline:genX} can get executed only once in between the two calls. Thus total runtime for each edge of the search tree is $O\left ( n \right )$.
nodes.statement_short: O(n) per tree edge, using Lemmas 10-11.

nodes.name: Total
nodes.statement: Note that the total number of calls made to the method method Enum-Uncertain-MC is no more than the possible number of unique subsets of $V$, which is $O \left ( 2^n \right )$. We see that for internal nodes, time complexity is $O \left ( n \right )$ and for leaf nodes it is $O \left ( 1 \right )$. Hence the time complexity of Algorithm~\ref{algo:dfs} is $O \left ( n \cdot 2^n \right )$.
nodes.statement_short: At most 2^n calls, so O(n 2^n).

nodes.name: Lines 1-6
nodes.statement: First note that lines 1-6 takes $O \left ( n \right )$ time. This is because $\left | I \right | = O \left ( n \right )$, and hence the loop at line 4 of Algorithm~\ref{algo:generateI} can take $O \left ( n \right )$ time. Further the set intersection at line 6 also takes $O \left ( n \right )$ time.
nodes.statement_short: Initial loop and intersection cost O(n).

nodes.name: Per-iteration goal
nodes.statement: We need to show that the for loop in line 7 is $O \left ( n \right )$, that is each iteration of the loop takes $O \left ( 1 \right )$ time.
nodes.statement_short: Remains: O(1) per iteration of the main loop.

nodes.name: Constant-time iteration
nodes.statement: Assume that it takes constant time to find out the probability of an edge. This is a valid assumption, as the edge probabilities can be stored as a HashMap and hence for an edge $e$, in constant time we can find out $p(e)$. With this assumption, it is easy to show that lines 8-13 takes constant time. This is because, they are either constant number of multiplications, or adding one element to a set.
nodes.statement_short: With hash-map edge lookups each iteration is O(1).

nodes.name: Total
nodes.statement: Thus total time complexity is $O \left ( n \right )$.
nodes.statement_short: Total O(n).

nodes.name: Small cliques not enumerated
nodes.statement: First we prove that no maximal clique of size less than $t$ is enumerated by Algorithm~\ref{algo:large}. Consider an $\alpha$-maximal clique $C_1$ in $\mathcal{G}$ with less than $t$ vertices. Also let $m_1 = \max(C_1)$ and $C_1' = C_1 \setminus \{ m_1 \}$. Note that if $C_1$ is emitted by Algorithm~\ref{algo:large}, then a call must be made to Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with $C_1$. Since the Algorithm adds vertices in lexicographical ordering, this implies that a call must be made to Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with $C_1'$ before the call is made with $C_1$. In the worst case, let us consider that the search tree reaches the execution point where Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large is called with $C_1'$. Consider the execution of the algorithm where $m_1$ is added to $C = C_1'$ to form $C' = C_1$. Since $C_1$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique, $I'$ will become NULL which implies $\left | I' \right | = 0$. We know that $\left | C_1 \right | < t$. Thus $\left | C_1 + I' \right |$ will also be less than $t$ and the If condition (line 8) will succeed. This will result in the execution of the continue statement. Thus Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large will not be called with $C_1$ implying that $C_1$ is not enumerated.
nodes.statement_short: A maximal clique with fewer than t vertices is cut by the size test.

nodes.name: Small clique and its prefix
nodes.statement: Consider an $\alpha$-maximal clique $C_1$ in $\mathcal{G}$ with less than $t$ vertices. Also let $m_1 = \max(C_1)$ and $C_1' = C_1 \setminus \{ m_1 \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a small maximal clique C_1 and C_1 minus its max.

nodes.name: Call must pass through prefix
nodes.statement: Note that if $C_1$ is emitted by Algorithm~\ref{algo:large}, then a call must be made to Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with $C_1$. Since the Algorithm adds vertices in lexicographical ordering, this implies that a call must be made to Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with $C_1'$ before the call is made with $C_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Emitting C_1 requires a call via C_1'.

nodes.name: Consider the extension step
nodes.statement: In the worst case, let us consider that the search tree reaches the execution point where Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large is called with $C_1'$. Consider the execution of the algorithm where $m_1$ is added to $C = C_1'$ to form $C' = C_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Look at adding m_1 to C_1'.

nodes.name: Size test fires
nodes.statement: Since $C_1$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique, $I'$ will become NULL which implies $\left | I' \right | = 0$. We know that $\left | C_1 \right | < t$. Thus $\left | C_1 + I' \right |$ will also be less than $t$ and the If condition (line 8) will succeed.
nodes.statement_short: I' is empty and |C_1| < t, so the test succeeds.

nodes.name: Not enumerated
nodes.statement: This will result in the execution of the continue statement. Thus Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large will not be called with $C_1$ implying that $C_1$ is not enumerated.
nodes.statement_short: The branch is skipped.

nodes.name: Large cliques enumerated
nodes.statement: Next we show that any maximal clique of size at least $t$ is enumerated by Algorithm~\ref{algo:large}. Consider an $\alpha$-maximal clique $C_2$ in $\mathcal{G}$ of size at least $t$. We note that the ``If'' condition in line 8 is never satisfied in the search path ending with $C_2$ and hence a call is made to the method with Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with $C_2$. This is easy to see as whenever a call is made to Enum-Uncertain-MC-Large with any $C \subseteq C_2$, since $C_2$ is large, we always have $\left | C \right | + \left | I \right | \ge t$.
nodes.statement_short: Along the path to a large clique the test never fires.

nodes.name: Grow the clique
nodes.statement: The algorithm starts with a set of vertices $C$ (initialized to an empty set) that is an $\alpha$-clique and incrementally adds vertices to $C$, while retaining the property of $C$ being an $\alpha$-clique, until we can add no more vertices to $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Start from the empty alpha-clique and add vertices while it stays an alpha-clique.

nodes.name: Report maximal clique
nodes.statement: At this point, we have an $\alpha$-maximal clique.

nodes.name: Backtrack
nodes.statement: Upon finding a clique that is $\alpha$-maximal, the algorithm backtracks to explore other possible vertices that can be used to extend $C$, until all possible search paths have been explored.
nodes.statement_short: Backtrack to explore the other extensions.

nodes.name: Increasing-id order
nodes.statement: To avoid exploring the same set $C$ more than once, we add vertices in increasing order of the vertex id. For instance, if $C$ was currently the vertex set $\{1,3,4\}$, we do not consider adding vertex $2$ to $C$, since the resulting clique $\{1,2,3,4\}$ will also be reached by the search path by adding vertices $1,2,3,4$ in that order.
nodes.statement_short: Add vertices only in increasing id order to avoid repeats.
